summary: One turn in a transcript — who, when, what, and what can be done with it. An article named by its author and time; never a live region.
useWhen: a conversation with an assistant, shown as a thread of turns
a transcript people read back — a support chat, a review thread between a person and an agent

useInstead.when: the entries are changes to a record — who changed what, when
useInstead.why: that is history, read as an ordered list of events; a transcript is turns people and an assistant took

useInstead.when: an agent is working through steps now
useInstead.why: a run has a live status per step; a message holds what was said

useInstead.when: a system message tells the reader something went wrong or changed
useInstead.why: an alert has an intent and a title; a message from a "System" author reads as a turn nobody took

composition.note: One ChatMessage per turn, in the order they were taken, oldest first. `from="person"` for what a person typed, `from="assistant"` for the reply. The assistant's content is the AssistantAnswer pattern: a StreamingText with Citations, then a CitationList and an Alert when degraded. `actions` follow the content — Copy, Ask again — as Buttons. Say when an answer is ready once, from a status region outside the messages, never from each message.
composition.example:
<ChatMessage from="person" author="Ada Reyes" avatar={<AvatarGradient size="sm" initials="AR" alt="Ada Reyes" />} timestamp={askedAt}>What is our refund limit?</ChatMessage>
<ChatMessage from="assistant" author="Ionbase assistant" avatar={<LogoMark size="sm" label="Ionbase assistant" />} timestamp={answeredAt} actions={<CopyButton value={text} label="Copy answer" />}><StreamingText isStreaming={false}>…</StreamingText></ChatMessage>

person.use: what a person wrote — on the trailing side, in a muted bubble at most 80% across

assistant.use: the assistant's reply — spans the column, since answers carry lists, sources and tables

author.note: the author's name, shown and read — the message's name starts with it

avatar.note: decoration, hidden from assistive tech; the name says who

children.accepts: text, StreamingText, Citation, CitationList, Alert, Link

actions.note: after the content, in reading order

guarantees: each message is an `<article>` named by its header — the author, then the time — so a screen reader moves message to message and hears who and when first
the time is a `<time>` with the exact instant as `dateTime`, whatever its label says
the avatar is hidden from assistive tech
it is not a live region: a thread never reads a streaming answer out as it arrives
the actions come after the content in the DOM, so Tab reaches a source in the answer before Copy
logical properties throughout, so right to left mirrors it
requires: `author` on every message, a person's included — "You" at the least
a status region outside the messages that says once when an answer is ready or incomplete
notes: It renders on a server. It holds a message; it does not send, stream or store one.

antiPatterns.why: a streaming answer is announced token by token, re-read with every chunk; announce completion once instead

antiPatterns.dont: a person's message in the primary tint
antiPatterns.why: the primary tint is AILabel's mark for generated content; a person's words must never read as generated

antiPatterns.dont: a message with only an avatar to say who wrote it
antiPatterns.why: the avatar is hidden from assistive tech, so the message has no author for anyone who cannot see it

antiPatterns.dont: a "System" message for an error or a notice
antiPatterns.why: it reads as a turn in the conversation, and it has no intent to say whether anything is wrong
